rv.q: New short works are due at the Almeida next year, and the National here revives her 1979 comedy about gender, sexuality and power structures, the first of her works to received serious attention.
A play which shouldn’t work, which should make us cringe with embarrassment, is an utter delight, delivered by a terrific cast and creative team who have worked wonders with the material.
All of it is gloriously good fun, with ideas about societal progress, both then and now, bubbling beneath it all.
In this lively production, Cooke makes Churchill’s satirical 1979 play feel brand new.
Cloud 9 is a remarkable piece of writing, and Cooke’s production gives it the space to ask questions that extend well beyond its original setting.

cn.t: Churchill's audacious play receives a superb National Theatre revival, with critics praising its unsettling yet accessible execution and Sam Troughton's show-stealing dual performance as both a five-year-old girl and hyper-masculine character.

ru.inst: Rush tickets released Fridays at 1 PM via National Theatre website (random queue).
